mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS above 4% for 3 months, or the 5-year rolling IC is above 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when controlling for lagged PAYEMS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% y/y for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which raises expected future profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative despite the 3-month CPIAUCSL acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month accompanied by a decline in inventory levels (not in the catalog, so omit interaction) suggests weakening supply chains, which can lead to higher inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO declines sharply.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 trading days due to persistent high discount rates eroding equity present value.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive during the high-rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (not in catalog) cannot be used; instead, a sharp rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a stable or declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) forms a labor market tightness signal that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >15% in a month while UNRATE remains below 4.5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are flat or negative despite strong payroll growth and low unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a post-recession expansion phase (as signaled by a combination of rising GDP proxies not available here, so using a proxy trigger instead) such as a 4-month rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain negative even during the rising INDPRO trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months suggests the Federal Reserve may pivot to rate cuts, lowering discount rates and supporting higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly inflation falls below 2% for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL < 2% for 3 months.
